status.title: Status
status.no_zones_description: Add a DNS zone to let other modules create and change its records.
status.audit_log_description: Every change to records and every call by another module is logged. Open the system logs, filtered on dnshelper audit.

action.list-provider-zones: List the zones of the DNS host

zones.title: Zones
zones.intro: A zone is a domain whose DNS records other modules may create and change, through your DNS host's API. Each zone uses a credential for its DNS host: usually an API token, for some hosts a key and secret or a user name and password.
zones.no_zones_description: Add a zone to get started.
zones.change_credential_help: Pick the credential the zone should use from now on. Records are not touched.
zones.remove_zone_description: Stop managing {zone}. Modules will no longer be able to change its records.
zones.remove_zone_explanation: The records at your DNS host are not deleted, and the credential is kept.
zones.removed: {zone} is no longer managed. Its records at your DNS host are unchanged.
zones.adopted_intro: Zones of the PowerDNS primary of this cluster are adopted automatically and kept in step with it. They cannot be changed or removed here; manage them in the PowerDNS module.
zones.sync_no_primary: There is no PowerDNS primary in this cluster. {removed} adopted zones removed.
zones.sync_skipped: Already configured here by hand, so not adopted: {zones}.
zones.sync_multiple: {modules} all claim to be the PowerDNS primary. Nothing was changed.
zones.remove_zone_snapshots: The zone's snapshot is deleted too. | The zone's {count} snapshots are deleted too.

records.title: Records
records.intro: View and change the records of a managed zone through dnshelper and the credential the zone uses. Changes are made at your DNS host at once. Before each change dnshelper keeps a snapshot of the zone, which Snapshots can compare with the zone and revert.
records.no_zones_description: Add a DNS zone first, then its records can be listed here.
records.no_records_description: This zone has no records at the DNS host.
records.add_help: The record is added to the zone at your DNS host. Existing records are not changed.
records.name_help: Relative to the zone: www for www.example.com, @ for the zone itself
records.ttl_help: Seconds. Leave empty for the DNS host's default; some hosts raise a very short TTL
records.invalid_ttl: Use a whole number of seconds
records.remove_description: Delete this record from {zone} at your DNS host:
records.remove_explanation: Other records with the same name are kept. Modules that rely on the record may stop working.
records.edit_help: The record is replaced in one change. If it was changed at the DNS host since this page was loaded, nothing is changed.
records.read_only_help: SOA and zone apex NS records are managed by the DNS host; dnshelper never changes them.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.intro: A credential is what your DNS host asks for to use its API: usually an API token, for some hosts a key and secret or a user name and password. One credential can serve several zones, and replacing it is a single edit. Secrets are never shown again after saving: leave a secret field empty to keep it. Prefer credentials limited to the zones you need.
credentials.no_credentials_description: A credential is created together with the first zone that uses it.
credentials.remove_description: Delete the credential {name}. It stays valid at your DNS host: revoke it there if it should no longer work.
credentials.removed: {name} is deleted here. It stays valid at your DNS host until you revoke it there.
credentials.saved: The changes to the credential are saved.
credentials.secret_help: Leave empty to keep the stored value

wizard.title: Add zone
wizard.provider_intro: Choose where the zone is hosted.
wizard.least_privilege: If your DNS host allows it, create a credential that can only edit the zones you add here, not your whole account. It is stored on this node and included in backups.
wizard.credential_name_help: A label for this credential, to recognise it later
wizard.zone_intro_listed: Choose one of the zones this credential can manage, or type its name.
wizard.zone_intro_typed: Type the name of the zone. This DNS host cannot list its zones.
wizard.find_zones: Find zones used by my modules
wizard.cannot_discover: Cannot look at the other modules
wizard.suggestions_help: Domains used by your mail, web server and other modules. Select one to use it.
wizard.validated_list-zones: The credential can see the zone at the DNS host.
wizard.validated_get-records: The credential can read the zone's records.
wizard.read_only: This DNS host cannot replace records through its API, so some changes by other modules may fail.
wizard.write_test_help: Optionally create and delete a temporary TXT record to prove that changes are allowed. Nothing else is touched.

access.title: Access
access.intro: Other modules change DNS records by calling dnshelper. A module can only do what a rule below allows: without a rule it is refused everything, even if it may call dnshelper. Administrators are not restricted by these rules.
access.roles_help: For a module to be allowed to call dnshelper at all, its image must declare this authorization (module developers set it in build-images.sh):
access.no_rules_description: No module can change records yet.
access.zones_help: Select the zones this rule applies to, or all zones.
access.zones_required: Select at least one zone, or all zones
access.caller_placeholder: Choose a module or type a pattern
access.caller_help: module/mail1, or a pattern such as module/mail*
access.names_help: Separated by commas, relative to the zone: @ is the zone itself, * matches anything, for example *._domainkey. Use * for all names.
access.types_help: Separated by commas, for example TXT, MX. Use * for all types (needed to delete without giving a type).
access.invalid_caller: Use module/ followed by the module id, like module/mail1
access.invalid_names: Use letters, digits, @, _, ., - and the wildcards * and ?
access.invalid_types: Use record types like TXT, or *
access.remove_description: Delete this rule for {caller}. The module will lose this access at once.

dns_error.not_permitted: Not allowed by the access rules
dns_error.zone_not_found: Zone not found at the DNS host, or not managed here
dns_error.auth_failed: The DNS host rejected the credential, or it has no access to this zone
dns_error.unsupported: This DNS host does not support that
dns_error.conflict: That would leave the zone invalid
dns_error.credential_in_use: The credential is still used by a zone
dns_error.managed_credential: This credential is adopted from PowerDNS and cannot be changed here
dns_error.managed_zone: This zone is adopted from PowerDNS and cannot be changed here
dns_error.leader_unreachable: The cluster leader cannot be reached; nothing was changed
dns_error.primary_unreachable: The PowerDNS primary did not answer; nothing was changed
dns_error.credential_id_taken: A credential with the id of the PowerDNS module already exists
dns_error.stale: The zone was changed since it was read; compare again

snapshots.title: Snapshots of {zone}
snapshots.intro: dnshelper keeps a snapshot of the zone before every change made through it, by this page or by another module, and when you take one here. Up to {count} snapshots per zone are kept, for {days} days; the latest is always kept. Retention is set on the Settings page.
snapshots.label: Label
snapshots.none_description: A snapshot is taken before the first change to this zone, or when you take one.
snapshots.same: The zone is the same as this snapshot; there is nothing to revert. SOA and apex NS records are not compared.
snapshots.revert_intro: These changes make the zone as it was in the snapshot. Untick any you want to keep as they are now. SOA and apex NS records are never changed.
snapshots.module_changes: Some of these records were written by another module after the snapshot (for example DKIM keys or certificate challenges). Reverting them may break that module until it writes them again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.snapshots_intro: dnshelper keeps a snapshot of a zone before every change made through it. Older snapshots are deleted when there are more than the maximum number, or when they are older than the maximum age; the latest snapshot of each zone is always kept. Snapshots are included in the module's backup.

record_form.host_help: A full host name, such as host.example.net
record_form.exchange_help: Host name of the mail server; a single . means this domain receives no mail
record_form.srv_target_help: Host name providing the service; must not be a CNAME. A single . means the service is not available
record_form.srv_name_hint: The record name says which service it is: for example _autodiscover._tcp or _imaps._tcp.
record_form.flags_help: Usually 0; 128 marks the tag as critical
record_form.caa_value_help: issue / issuewild: the certificate authority's domain, such as letsencrypt.org; iodef: a mailto: or https: URL for reports
record_form.txt_long: Longer than 255 bytes: it is split into several strings for you.
record_form.hint_spf: An SPF record. A name must have only one: put every mechanism in this record.
record_form.hint_dkim: A DKIM key. Paste the whole value as given by your mail server; line breaks are removed.
record_form.hint_dmarc: A DMARC policy. It belongs at the name _dmarc.
record_form.second_spf: {name} already has an SPF record. Two SPF records at one name make SPF checks fail: edit the existing one instead.
record_form.invalid_16bit: Use a whole number from 0 to 65535
record_form.invalid_flags: Use a whole number from 0 to 255
record_form.txt_quoted: Enter the plain value, without the surrounding quotes
record_form.ns_help: Delegates this name to other name servers, such as ns1.example.net. The zone's own name servers (at @) can't be changed here.
record_form.apex_ns: The zone's own NS records are managed by the DNS host and can't be changed here

pending.title: 1 pending change | {count} pending changes
pending.zone_locked: Apply or discard the pending changes before choosing another zone
pending.staged: 1 change is pending. | {count} changes are pending.
pending.skipped: 1 record was left out: it already has a pending change. | {count} records were left out: they already have a pending change.
pending.review_intro: These changes are made at your DNS host in one step. A snapshot of the zone is kept first, so they can be reverted.
pending.nothing: These changes would not change anything in the zone.
pending.split: There are more changes than one request takes, so they are applied in {parts} parts, one after the other. Each part is checked on its own: if one fails, the parts before it stay applied.
pending.label: Records page: 1 change | Records page: {count} changes
pending.applied: 1 change was applied. | {count} changes were applied.

bulk.ttl_intro: The {count} selected records get this TTL. Records that already have it are left as they are.
bulk.find_intro: Replace text in record values, for example to point every CNAME at a new host, or to change an address during a server move. Matching records are added to the pending changes; nothing is changed until you review and apply them.
bulk.name_pattern_help: * matches any characters, ? one; @ is the zone itself
bulk.matches: No records match | 1 record matches | {count} records match
bulk.stage: Add to pending changes | Add 1 change to pending changes | Add {count} changes to pending changes
